Hypothesis is `LinearIndependent A v` (independence over the algebra A), but the book requires the v_i linearly independent over the field k. In a simple A-module any two distinct nonzero vectors are A-dependent (A acts surjectively onto V from any nonzero vector), so `LinearIndependent A v` forces n ≤ 1; the proof literally `exfalso`s the n ≥ 2 case. Thus the theorem is non-vacuous only for n ≤ 1 and the genuine content (interpolation through arbitrarily many k-independent vectors) is unreachable. The hypothesis is far stronger than the book's, collapsing the statement.
